newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon banks to cut prime lending rate.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon banks to cut prime lending rate.

text.p: The Lebanese Banks Association said on Thursday it plans to cut the Lebanese pound prime lending rate to 16 percent from 18 percent soon, the second rate slash in five weeks in line with cuts in t-bill yields.
Banque Libano-Francaise, a major Beirut bank, said it began adhering to the new rate immediately, before the association announces it.
An official of the association grouping 79 of Lebanon's 82 banks said the rate cut was discussed at a meeting of its board on Tuesday and there was almost unanimous agreement to order it.
"We plan to lower the pound prime rate to 16 from 18 percent. The decision will be taken soon," Dr Makram Sader, the secretary-general of the association told Reuters.
In mid-January the association slashed the pound rate to 18 percent from 24 percent. The last cut before that was in January 1996, when the prime rate was lowered from 30 percent.
Sader said the cut would be in line with declining pound-denominated treasury bill yields and was also aimed at boosting lending in the local currency.
The prime rate is the borrowing rate which commercial banks charge to their best customers.
"This new cut is in line with the earlier one," Sader said.

"Firstly there is the falling treasury bill rates and secondly we aim at boosting lending in Lebanese pounds and thirdly to lower the competition between banks over foreign currency deposits," he added.

Yields on Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bills of three-month, six-month, one-year and two-year maturities for the February 20 issue are 13.87 percent, 14.64 percent, 15.33 percent and 16.18 percent respectively.
They were 14.61 percent, 16.92 percent, 17.78 percent and 21.62 percent four months ago.
An official at Banque Libano-Francaise confirmed a newspaper report which said that the bank has informed all its branches in Lebanon to stick to the new pound prime rate as of Thursday.
An Nahar daily said other banks, like Byblos Bank, Banque Audi and Banque du Liban et D'Outre-Mer, will follow suit soon.
Asked why the bank slashed the rate before the banks association ordered it, the bank official told Reuters: "We are following the market as t-bill yields are falling quickly".
He said the new prime rate -- which reduces the margin with dollar lending rates -- would encourage Lebanese to borrow more in their local currency.

"In the past, when you told a person that you would lend him Lebanese pounds at say 27 percent, he would decline as he could get a better dollar lending rate but now the pound rate is close to the dollar rates of 9-13 percent," the banker said.
The dollar prime rate for Lebanon's major commercial banks is 10.5 percent, according to the association.
Talal Abou Zaki, Manager Forex and Money Markets with Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, also said the rate cut would boost lending in Lebanese pounds a little.
